notes: Qualitative finding (no values): Silage spores survive pasteurization and germinate during ripening: late blowing and unpleasant odor. It is prevented without silage (Parmigiano Reggiano), with bactofugation, nisin, nitrate or lysozyme.

Qualitative finding (no values): Their heat-stable lipases and proteases survive pasteurization; they cause excessive lipolysis and proteolysis, with rancid, fruity and bitter flavors. In Cottage, the diacetyl reductase of Pseudomonas removes diacetyl and leaves a flat flavor.

pathway_according_to_source: Citrate metabolism by LAB (citrate+ Lactococcus lactis, Leuconostoc) → diacetyl, acetoin, acetate, CO₂
notes: Qualitative finding (no values): CO₂ forms the small eyes of Edam and Gouda; diacetyl and acetate give the flavor of Quarg, Fromage frais and Cottage.

pathway_according_to_source: Citrate metabolism by LAB (citrate+ Lactococcus lactis, Leuconostoc) → diacetyl, acetoin, acetate, CO₂
notes: Qualitative finding (no values): Acceptable diacetyl ≈ 2 ppm. Ratio 3–5: good flavor; > 5: "harsh"; < 3: "green".
Qualitative finding (no values): With S/M below 4%, mature Cheddar tends to develop gas and sulfide flavors; bitterness increases as S/M decreases.

pathway_according_to_source: Butyric fermentation: lactate → butyric acid + CO₂ + H₂ (Clostridium tyrobutyricum)
notes: Qualitative finding (no values): About 50 spores per liter of milk are enough. In Switzerland, Emmental is made with milk from cows not fed silage; bactofugation, microfiltration, nitrate, lysozyme or nisin also work (these are not allowed in Switzerland). Clostridium sporogenes gives intense proteolysis with putrid spots.

Qualitative finding (no values): Normally there are 2–7 g/kg of FFA (mainly from propionibacteria); more give rancidity, caused mainly by butyric and caproic acids. Lipases from the flora of poorly stored raw milk also contribute.

pathway_according_to_source: Proteolysis: phenylalanine → cinnamic acid → styrene (phenylalanine ammonia lyase of P. camemberti)
notes: Qualitative finding (no values): When P. camemberti depletes lactose and lactate (ripening > 15 °C, washed curd or high fat) it attacks proteins and fat and produces styrene; only certain strains.

pathway_according_to_source: Catabolism of unsaturated fatty acids by Penicillium
notes: Qualitative finding (no values): Mushroom notes (1-octen-3-ol, 3-octanone), geranium (1,5-octadien-3-one and -3-ol), earth (2-methylisoborneol) and potato (2-methoxy-3-isopropylpyrazine). Mushroom is desirable at a low level and a defect at a high level.
Qualitative finding (no values): The pungent and "sharp" flavor of blue cheese comes from short-chain FFA and methyl ketones; esters and lactones explain the variation between varieties.

cheese_label_raw: Blue cheese, Camembert, Cheddar, processed cheese
cheese_name_std: Blue cheese, Camembert, Cheddar, processed cheese
notes: Qualitative finding (no values): Soapy flavor is associated with high FFA, especially C10 and C12; it increases with added lipases or molds and with homogenization of the milk or cream.

other_process_factor_raw: pH > 5,0; brine with less salt than the cheese
compound_or_family_raw: Sulfur compounds (cooked cabbage, rotten egg odor)
notes: Qualitative finding (no values): On opening the package it smells of cooked cabbage due to sulfur compounds; if the defect advances, rotten egg. It is prevented with pH < 5.0 at 24 h, moisture ≤ 58% and adequate salt.

cheese_label_raw: Cheddar, Swiss, blue, grana/pecorino, Camembert, Cottage, Limburger…
cheese_name_std: Cheddar, Swiss, blue, grana/pecorino, Camembert, Cottage, Limburger…

cited_primary_source_raw: Adda & Dumont (1974); Urbach (1993); Singh et al. (2003)
notes: Qualitative finding (no values): Table 19.1: impact compound by variety — Cheddar: methanethiol; Swiss: 3-methylbutyric and propionic acids; blue cheeses: heptan-2-one; grana and pecorino: n-butyric acid; Camembert: 1-octen-3-ol; Cottage: diacetyl and acetaldehyde; Limburger and Tilsit: methanethiol, thioesters and H₂S.

Qualitative finding (no values): Aroma value of 4-ethyloctanoate > 1400 in goat milk and cheeses and > 200 in sheep; less than 0.1% (goat) or 0.5% (sheep) of these acids in free form is enough to give the goaty flavor. Whatever favors or prevents their release determines the flavor.

Qualitative finding (no values): Methyl ketones are the most abundant volatiles (25–60 mmol per 100 g of fat), especially nonan-2-one and heptan-2-one; together with their secondary alcohols they make up 10–20% and 5–10% of the aromas. 1-Octen-3-ol partially masks the blue note of the methyl ketones.
Qualitative finding (no values): Sulfur compounds appeared only in aged Camembert with B. linens growth.
Qualitative finding (no values): The L. paracasei adjunct gives more alcohols, acetoin, lactones, 2-phenylethanol and phenylacetaldehyde.

Qualitative finding (no values): Low-fat Cheddar develops "meaty–brothy" or "burnt–brothy" flavor (furanones and methional), "burnt" (1-octen-3-one) and "rosy" (phenylacetaldehyde); the buttery, creamy and caramel notes decrease.

compound_or_family_raw: Acids, esters and lactones; pentanoic acid, 2-methylpropanoic acid
notes: Qualitative finding (no values): The raw-milk cheese had more acids, esters and lactones, and fewer aldehydes and sulfur compounds, than the pasteurized one.

compound_or_family_raw: Ethyl esters, isoamyl acetate, phenylethyl acetate
notes: Qualitative finding (no values): Ripening in a wooden barrel gave more ethyl acetate, butanoate, hexanoate, octanoate, lactate and decanoate, 3-methylbutyl acetate and phenylethyl acetate.

cited_primary_source_raw: Morales et al. (2003); O'Sullivan et al. (2013)
notes: Qualitative finding (no values): Lactococci that produce ethyl esters give a defective fruity flavor; its overgrowth gives "harsh green" and alcoholic flavors from methanol and acetaldehyde.

Qualitative finding (no values): Fig. 3.2: FFA range from ~700 mg/kg (Brie, Edam) to > 32,000 mg/kg (Roquefort, Danish Blue, Parmesan). In Camembert and blue cheeses FFA are not perceived as rancid because of the high pH; at high pH the anions are perceived as soap.

condition: Goat and sheep milk vs cow milk
notes: Qualitative finding (no values): Caproic and caprylic acids are higher in goat milk, and caprylic in sheep milk; in sheep, C8 and C10 almost double those of cow and in goat C10 triples it.

condition: Detoxification of FFA by the mold
pathway_according_to_source: Lipolysis: β-oxidation → methyl ketones (one carbon fewer + CO₂) → secondary alcohols
notes: Qualitative finding (no values): FFA are toxic to the mold, which β-oxidizes and decarboxylates them to methyl ketones; Penicillium reduces acetone, 2-heptanone and 2-nonanone to 2-pentanol, 2-heptanol and 2-nonanol.
Qualitative finding (no values): Lactones are higher in Parmesan and Grana Padano because of their high cooking temperatures; diet, season, lactation and breed influence their formation in milk.
Qualitative finding (no values): Citrate gives CO₂, diacetyl and acetoin: open texture and the characteristic flavor of Svecia.

Qualitative finding (no values): With wooden utensils the aroma profile was richer; several compounds did not appear in the copper or steel cheese.

compound_or_family_raw: Branched-chain aldehydes and alcohols; diacetyl and acetoin
notes: Qualitative finding (no values): The adjunct gave more branched-chain aldehydes and alcohols and less diacetyl and acetoin.

notes: Qualitative finding (no values): Terpenes serve as grazing markers in humid European grasslands.
Qualitative finding (no values): Pasteurization inactivates 73–95% of lipoprotein lipase; raw-milk cheeses ripen faster and give stronger flavors.
Qualitative finding (no values): In full-fat Cheddar the methyl ketones increase for 14 weeks and then decrease; in the low-fat cheese they reach 25% of those of the full-fat cheese.

notes: Qualitative finding (no values): The adjunct increased diacetyl and acetoin, raised flavor and odor intensity, and lowered the pungent taste and the rancidity compounds.

Qualitative finding (no values): Roncal is made with milk from transhumant sheep; hard raw-milk cheese, acidified by the natural microflora, cooked, smoked and ripened for 7 weeks.
